thread:
alice_support: Hi team — customer (AcmeFin) reporting SSO failures after scheduled IdP cert rotation this morning. Getting 403 on ACS POST and AssertionRecipientMismatch in logs. Can SRE help triage? :eyes:

bob_sre: Looking. Do we have the full authz error? Customer shared a screenshot?

alice_support: They pasted this snippet from our proxy: `Assertion failed: recipient mismatch (expected https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs, got https://acme.example.com/sso/acs)` and reported 403s right after cert swap at 06:12 UTC. Also see `InvalidSignature` in some requests.

carol_engineer: Two likely things: (1) IdP metadata published new cert and maybe changed <AssertionConsumerService> endpoint ordering or URL (2) RelayState or host header rewrite at the edge. Any chance the IdP returned an ACS with the customer's own host instead of our configured url?

bob_sre: I pulled edge logs. We proxied to internal acs handler but reject happened upstream in SAML validator: log shows `AssertionRecipientMismatch: recipient="https://acme.example.com/sso/acs" expected="https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs"`. That suggests IdP used SP entity alias in Assertion. Could be IdP attribute mapping changed.

alice_support: Customer (dave_customer) chiming in: "We rotated an intermediate yesterday and our IdP team updated metadata. We didn't change SP config. We see the Assertion's Recipient set to our app URL, but we also see a different EntityID in the Issuer. We tried reimporting metadata into your tenant but still 403s."

dave_customer: additional note — on our side the IdP shows two ACS entries: one with trailing slash and one without: `https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs` and `https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs/`. We didn't expect that.

carol_engineer: Trailing slash mismatches are common. Our validator canonicalizes but only if entityIDs match. The `expected` value in our config is `https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs` (no trailing slash). If the Assertion uses the slash variant AND the Assertion's Recipient header is used with exact match, we might reject. However the earlier log where recipient was the customer's host is more concerning.

erin_idp_admin: From IdP POV: we deployed cert rotation and during the replay some metadata fetches got cached older entityID mapping. We pushed metadata with multiple KeyDescriptor entries and reordered ACS list to include the customer's host as first entry to support vanity domains. That explains why Assertion sometimes uses acme.example.com.

bob_sre: OK that'll do it. Our smart routing policy pins SP entityID to tenant config. When IdP sends a different ACS first we still accept it only if the SubjectConfirmationData Recipient matches one of the configured ACS endpoints for that SP. The mismatch to acme.example.com fails. Two fixes: have IdP ensure Assertion uses the canonical ACS URL we provide, or we add the alias host as an allowed ACS for this tenant. Which does Acme prefer?

dave_customer: We prefer to support vanity host but we didn't realize it would break your strict check. We can update our IdP to put the canonical ACS first. We also can add the alias in your tenant if you accept.

alice_support: Action items: 1) Carol — can you patch temporary allowlist for acme.example.com as ACS for this tenant so they can proceed? 2) Erin/dave — reorder ACS in IdP metadata to put canonical URL first and re-export signed metadata. 3) Bob — add a note to docs about ACS ordering + cert rotation gotcha.

carol_engineer: I'll add alias to tenant allowlist now. Doing `PATCH /admin/tenants/acme/ssoconfig` with allowed_acs array — example: ```json
{"allowed_acs": ["https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs","https://app.redwood.ai/sso/acs/","https://acme.example.com/sso/acs"]}``` Should be quick. Will monitor logs.

deploy_bot: deploy started: egress-config patch v2.14 -> staging (carol_engineer)

carol_engineer: Patch applied to staging and prod within minutes. I see successful POSTs from IdP now and no AssertionRecipientMismatch in recent logs. Still seeing occasional `InvalidSignature` for a small fraction (~2%) — likely some metadata signed with old intermediate.

erin_idp_admin: We'll re-publish metadata with full chain and cache-bust URL (add ?v=2) to avoid stale fetches. Also will ensure ordering.

bob_sre: Thanks. I'll keep monitors for 2 hours. If InvalidSignature persists beyond the cache TTL, we'll escalate. For follow-up: document recommended metadata roll procedure (update metadata, ensure full cert chain, keep alias entries, rotate during low traffic).

alice_support: Thanks everyone — looping customer: @dave_customer you should be unblocked. Please confirm and close the ticket when green. :thumbsup:

dave_customer: Confirmed — SSO working for all users after patch. We'll do metadata reorder + re-publish. Appreciate the fast turnaround!

alice_support: Closing notes: root cause = IdP metadata reorder during cert rotation exposing alias ACS as first entry + partial propagation of new cert chain causing intermittent InvalidSignature. Remediation = tenant allowlist + proper metadata publishing steps. Will convert to KB article.
